originality.rationale: Primary paper [1, Corollary 1.13] proves only L2 radial thin-shell concentration; [1, Section 3.3] proves fixed-order exact moments, and [1, Section 2.1] gives Gaussian-probe identities. Neither the central limit distribution nor the uniform transform estimate (3) is stated there. The new theorem needs dimension-uniform beta-exponential control and full characteristic functions. Panzo–Socher [3] studies other expected geometric functionals; inspected public research findings concern different random objects/observables. This is substantive new asymptotic information, though general historical priority is not certified.
residual_risks: A general high-dimensional analytic-transform CLT could imply the result if it applies to these specific Brownian hull expected-volume measures; none was found in the examined sources.

Indexed search and inspected sources cannot establish worldwide historical priority; independent literature review is outstanding.

value.rationale: The volume-annealed Brownian hull thin shells were identified at only L2 law-of-large-numbers precision. The proved CLTs resolve the natural next-order distribution of precisely that canonical random point and show both types have a common standardized variance 22/5, versus 2 for their Gaussian time-average proxies. The strict 11/5 variance ratio reveals nontrivial hull geometry not determined by radii, fixed two moments, or generic Gaussian concentration. It is not a parameter renaming, trivial first-moment calculation, or unrelated slice.
